hints: Use integration by parts with $u=x^2$ and $dv=\cos(x/3)\,dx$.
After the first step, integrate the remaining $x\sin(x/3)$ term by parts again, differentiating $x$.
Check the chain-rule factors when integrating $\cos(x/3)$ and $\sin(x/3)$, and simplify the full antiderivative before applying limits.
Substitute $x=\pi$ and $x=0$ using $\sin(\pi/3)=\sqrt3/2$ and $\cos(\pi/3)=1/2$, then keep the result exact.
walkthrough:
Apply integration by parts $\int u\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}\,\mathrm{d}x = uv - \int v\dfrac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}\,\mathrm{d}x$ with $u = x^2$ and $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x} = \cos\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} = 2x, \quad v = 3\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$$
$$\int x^2\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x = x^2\left(3\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\right) - \int 3\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)(2x)\,\mathrm{d}x$$
$$= 3x^2\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) - \int 6x\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Apply integration by parts a second time to the integral $\int 6x\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x$:
$$u_1 = 6x \implies \dfrac{\mathrm{d}u_1}{\mathrm{d}x} = 6$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v_1}{\mathrm{d}x} = \sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) \implies v_1 = -3\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$$
$$\int 6x\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x = (6x)\left(-3\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\right) - \int \left(-3\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\right)(6)\,\mathrm{d}x$$
$$= -18x\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) + \int 18\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x$$
$$= -18x\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) + 18\left(3\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\right)$$
$$= -18x\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) + 54\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$$

Combine the two integration steps to write the complete antiderivative:
$$\int x^2\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x = 3x^2\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) - \left[-18x\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) + 54\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\right]$$
$$= 3x^2\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) + 18x\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) - 54\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$$

Evaluate the antiderivative at the upper limit $x = \pi$:
$$\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, \quad \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$$
$$3(\pi)^2\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + 18(\pi)\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) - 54\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$$
$$= \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}\pi^2 + 9\pi - 27\sqrt{3}$$

Evaluate the antiderivative at the lower limit $x = 0$:
$$3(0)^2\sin(0) + 18(0)\cos(0) - 54\sin(0) = 0 + 0 - 0 = 0$$

Subtract the lower limit value from the upper limit value to obtain the final exact value:
$$\int_0^\pi x^2\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x = \left(\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}\pi^2 + 9\pi - 27\sqrt{3}\right) - 0 = \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}\pi^2 + 9\pi - 27\sqrt{3}$$
